name: Building Engines on AI in Commercial Real Estate Operations
title: Building Engines on AI in Commercial Real Estate Operations
answer: Building Engines publishes a commercial real estate operations website whose Prism product pages, guide, blog article and case study describe AI uses in property management. The most useful single point is that Prism AI connects to live work orders, preventive maintenance schedules, equipment records and documents, then answers plain English questions and recommends actions, while JLL research cited in its guide says 90% of organizations plan to increase AI investments over five years but only 20% of property managers currently use AI in building operations.

sections.body: Building Engines publishes this commercial real estate operations website. The material includes product pages for Prism AI, Prism Preventive Maintenance, Prism Insights, building communications, Prism Operations and the platform overview, plus a homepage, a resource landing page for a practical guide to AI in commercial real estate, a blog article on intelligent buildings after COVID, and a case study on certificate of insurance tracking. The pages describe software for property teams. The site cites G2 Grid Summer 2026 and JLL research, while the blog refers to fourth quarter 2021 and a Forrester survey described as last year.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: Building Engines describes Prism AI as an add-on workflow within its Prism platform that turns operational data and documents into conversational answers, automated workflows and predictive insights. It says users can ask about average work order response time, get troubleshooting advice from equipment manuals, compare inspection reports, review vendor contracts for billing issues, automate invoice entry and data analysis, and analyze work order patterns, equipment performance and maintenance schedules to catch problems before costly repairs. Prism AI is built on JLL Falcon, trained on proprietary commercial real estate data and connected to work orders, preventive maintenance schedules, equipment records, documents and tenant satisfaction scores. The preventive maintenance page says AI can analyze service histories to spot repeat failures, prioritize repairs by make, model and age, turn manuals into step-by-step instructions and recommend maintenance frequencies based on actual usage rather than manufacturer defaults. The communications page says AI reviews outgoing tenant messages for inappropriate or unprofessional language and alerts the sender while leaving the decision to property teams. Prism Insights refreshes dashboards hourly and lets users ask questions in plain English. The platform overview says Prism accelerates certificate of insurance compliance with automated collection, AI-powered verification and insurance expert review. The guide cites JLL research that 90% of organizations plan to increase AI investments over five years and only 20% of property managers currently use AI in building operations. The blog defines intelligent buildings and says energy efficiency and sustainability technology can cut 20% off annual energy costs.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Building Engines says emergency repairs cost 3 to 4 times more than scheduled maintenance. It says Prism AI is SOC 2 Type II certified with AES 256 encryption and complete data segregation, is built on AWS with AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit, supports GDPR, CCPA and single sign-on with Office 365, Active Directory and Okta, and deletes inactive conversations after 32 days. It says property, tenant and financial data is never shared across organizations or used to train AI models. The guide cites JLL research that 90% of organizations plan to increase AI investments over the next five years and only 20% of property managers currently use AI in building operations. The blog cites a Forrester survey in which 80% of top commercial real estate decision-makers said they would spend more on real estate technology, and says energy efficiency and sustainability technology can cut 20% off annual energy costs. The homepage says property teams managing more than 6 billion square feet use the platform. The case study describes a team managing 500 active and expiring certificates of insurance plus certificates for 80 tenants, and an assistant general manager using Jones for 31 tenants at a Manhattan building. The operations page says Prism combines more than 20 years of CRE operations expertise.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in real estate, this source is useful as a vendor's detailed account of where AI is being applied in commercial property operations. It shows concrete workflows: conversational querying of work orders and leases, predictive maintenance, document review, tenant message screening and insurance certificate verification. It also gives a market adoption contrast through JLL research, with most organizations planning more AI investment while only a minority of property managers use it in building operations. The blog adds a definition of intelligent buildings and a claim about energy savings. The case study shows AI-assisted insurance compliance in practice. The material helps readers compare vendor claims and identify operational use cases, though it is not independent evidence of results.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Real Estate

sections.body: This is commercial vendor content from Building Engines, so it presents Prism and related products favorably and does not offer independent benchmarks, customer outcome data beyond one case study, or implementation failures. Many pages are product descriptions rather than research. The guide is a resource landing page with limited detail. The blog article is dated by its references to the pandemic and fourth quarter 2021. The case study concerns Jones software, not Prism AI, though it appears on the Building Engines site. Pricing is available only upon request, and most pages do not state publication dates.
